clue.text: Woman outside the "Ram's Head" will be quarrelsome

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it, so the woman's word encloses the next piece
the head of a word is its first letter, so only the front of Ram is kept

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman
the opening letter of Ram
will as a noun means desire or wish

explanation.surface: A woman standing outside a pub called the Ram's Head is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the Ram's Head look like a pub name; only the ram's first letter counts, and 'will' is the noun meaning a desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging person, so shrewish describes someone given to scolding and quarrels.

clue.text: Employed you, me and Mr Rusbridger

blocks.note: you and me together are us
Alan Rusbridger was editor of the Guardian, and ED abbreviates editor

explanation.surface: A boast that the setter, the solver and the newspaper's boss all work for the same paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Rusbridger edited the Guardian, which published this puzzle, so he stands for ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Used and employed are synonyms in the sense of something having been put to work or service.

clue.text: Take out famous horse for a turn

indicators.note: turning something round sends it back the other way, so the horse's name is read from the end

blocks.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, the great British steeplechase, three times

explanation.surface: Someone proposes taking a celebrated racehorse out for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the famous horse; the name famously spells the answer backwards, as used in the film The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is slang for killing them, which is exactly what this word means as a verb.

clue.text: Chap mainly rents accommodation to soldiers

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Bill is a man's name, so a chap
to let a room is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A man rents most of his rooms out to soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill loses his last L before LETS joins on, so the double L comes from one in each piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Billets are lodgings assigned to soldiers, often in private houses, so they are quarters given to troops.

clue.text: Blasting unfit accommodation for horses

indicators.note: something unfit is in poor shape, so these letters are knocked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone condemns horse quarters by blasting them as unfit to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabling is the collective term for stables, the buildings where horses are housed.

clue.text: Hobby turned into career

indicators.note: something turned has been changed into another form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A pastime that someone has managed to make into a full-time job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned into' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'into' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is any leisure pursuit done for enjoyment, which is what a hobby is.

clue.text: Shrub seed contains disease

indicators.note: a word that contains another holds it inside, so the seed's letters wrap around the illness

blocks.note: a pea is a seed from a pod
rot is a decay disease of plants

explanation.surface: A gardener warns that the seed of some bush is carrying a plant disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a South African evergreen bush with large showy flowerheads, the national flower there.

clue.text: Books in translation are thus international

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
I is the standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A claim that books available in translation are by that fact international.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri, the plural of thesaurus, are reference books listing synonyms, so they are a kind of book.

clue.text: Originally hers, it belongs to them

definitions.note: read as 'it is ___', the answer is what belongs to them

indicators.note: done originally means done in a novel way, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Something that once belonged to her is now owned by them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' wants to mean first letters, giving H alone; instead it asks for the letters of 'hers, it' in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means something owned by those people, so if it belongs to them it is said to be this.

clue.text: They say chap would take notice

indicators.note: what they say is what is heard spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a chap is he, and he would contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a certain man would pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to pay attention to it, a synonym for taking notice.

clue.text: Careful chap gets single reprimand

blocks.note: Del is short for Derek, a man's name
the Roman numeral one
to berate is to scold

explanation.surface: A cautious man receives just one telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate describes slow, unhurried, considered action, a synonym of careful.

clue.text: Refuse to give birth

blocks.note: first meaning: rubbish dropped in public places
second meaning: to bear a brood of young, as a cat or dog does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish, stressed on the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for scattered rubbish and a verb for animals producing a batch of young.

clue.text: Groups of experts concentrate on military hardware

blocks.note: to concentrate is to think hard
tanks are armoured fighting vehicles

explanation.surface: Specialist panels focus their attention on weapons and armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Think tanks are bodies of specialists who research and advise on policy problems.

clue.text: Adjust sail approaching these islands in boat

blocks.note: to trim a sail is to adjust it to the wind
the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A sailor tweaks the canvas while nearing a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with three parallel hulls.

clue.text: Conducted meeting about hospital broadcast

blocks.note: C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
H is the map symbol for hospital
a programme that is aired has been broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone ran a session about a hospital that went out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, so this past tense means ran or presided over one.

clue.text: Stretch out one leg at dance

indicators.note: dancing sends things moving into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A dancer is told to extend a single leg during the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to make longer, which is what stretching something out does.

clue.text: One gets impatient at last in opposition

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a means one
to gain is to get
the closing letter of impatient

explanation.surface: Someone finally loses patience about being outvoted by the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to oppose it, so the word means in opposition to.

clue.text: Not quite resisting terrible evil

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter goes
something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the word missing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is barely holding out against some dreadful wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something menacing or wicked, a close synonym of evil.

clue.text: Sculpture's about right height

indicators.note: about means around, so the sculpture's word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: a statue is a piece of sculpture
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A statue appears to be just about the correct size.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural height when standing.

clue.text: Detectives finally remove surveillance

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the closing letter of Detectives
to take out is to remove

explanation.surface: Police at last call off their watch on a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs detectives with surveillance, but detectives supply only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a period of secret watching of a place or person, typically by police.

clue.text: Temperature perhaps suits some Africans

indicators.note: perhaps hints at a possible alternative version, so these letters may be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: T abbreviates temperature
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A remark that the warm weather probably suits people in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsis are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi, so they are some of Africa's peoples.

clue.text: A number of extremely nebulous projections

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: ten is a number
O' is a shortened of, as in o'clock
the first and last letters of nebulous

explanation.surface: Some unspecified number of hazy, ill-defined protrusions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of wood that fits into a mortise joint.

clue.text: Holy books in Tibetan translation

definitions.note: the answer is singular in form but names a body of sacred texts

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Sacred scriptures available in a Tibetan-language version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation' wants to be an anagram signal, but the letters are read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantra is a body of Hindu and Buddhist scriptures, so it names a set of sacred texts.

clue.text: Untidy things are firstly to be put in order

indicators.note: an untidy set of things is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled
firstly points to the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the opening letter of to

explanation.surface: Messy belongings should be the first things tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a room is to tidy it, setting things neatly in their places.

clue.text: Tom is soppy about girl

indicators.note: about here means within the area of, so the letters sit across the preceding words

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word runs through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A boy called Tom is sentimental over a girl he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' usually signals going around; here the letters simply lie across the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title and old-fashioned term for a young unmarried woman or girl.

clue.text: Girl's crazy about you, we hear

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for crazy wraps the next piece
what we hear is spoken, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: mad means crazy
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A girl confesses she is wild about the person she is speaking to.
explanation.definitionFit: Maud is a girl's name, as in Tennyson's poem Come into the garden, Maud.

clue.text: Choose European team's No 1 as striker

indicators.note: number one in a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
E abbreviates European
the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: A manager selects a European side's best player to play up front.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like football, where a striker is a forward; here the striker is a worker on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a person standing outside a workplace during industrial action, so a striker.

clue.text: Diverted engineers take complicated detour

indicators.note: a complicated thing is tangled, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Traffic has been sent by army engineers on a convoluted diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute traffic is to send it by a different road, the same as diverting it.
